issues.body: `_model_container_binds` recognizes mount options only when the flag and specification occur as literal source tokens. `_run_headless_harness` can instead assign, for example, `local registry_flag=--volume registry_spec="$SCRIPT_DIR/..:/registry"` and place `"$registry_flag" "$registry_spec"` in the initial `container=(...)` array. This is valid shell and gives Docker a writable bind of the registry checkout, but the awk scanner ignores both the assignments and expansions, still emits exactly the four expected records, and the `container+=(` assertion still sees one append. The synthetic fixture covers literal mount syntaxes only, so it does not close the composition seam recorded in round 4.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the effective argv passed to Docker, or tightly constrain and structurally validate every construct that can produce launcher-array elements, including scalar/array/function/command-substitution expansion. Add a valid, non-crashing mutant that builds `--volume` and its specification in variables and expands them into the initial `container` array, and require the containment assertion to fail. A lexical inventory of literal Docker spellings cannot establish an exact runtime argv contract.
issues.title: Exact mount assertion still misses shell-composed Docker arguments

verdict.summary: The round-4 blocker remains. `_model_container_binds` still scans literal whitespace-delimited source tokens inside `_run_headless_harness`; it does not validate the effective Docker argv after shell expansion. The launcher can assign a mount flag and writable registry bind specification to shell variables and expand them into the initial `container=(...)` array. Docker then receives the registry mount, while this awk scan emits only the four expected literal records and the separate `container+=(` count remains one. The added mutants and syntax fixture exercise literal Docker spellings but not shell-composed arguments. This is materially the same blocker at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
